questions.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=(x+y)\,i+(y-x)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =x+y=3(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t), \\ Q(x,y) & =y-x=3(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(3(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t))\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(3(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t))\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({cos}^{2}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }1\,\text{d}t \\  & =9t{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =9(2\pi -0) \\  & =18\pi \end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=xy\,i+{x}^{2}\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =xy=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & ={x}^{2}=4{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(4{cos}^{2}⁡t)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }16\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{1}-16{u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & ={e}^{y}={e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t}, \\ Q(x,y) & ={e}^{x}={e}^{3\operatorname{cos}⁡t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitutions $u=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,du=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt$ and $v=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,dv=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t})\cdot (4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-({e}^{3\operatorname{cos}⁡t})\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t})\cdot (4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({e}^{3\operatorname{cos}⁡t})\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{0}{e}^{u}\,du-{\int }_{1}^{1}{e}^{v}\,\text{d}v \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=y\,i+9{x}^{3}\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =9{x}^{3}=9{cos}^{3}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $\operatorname{cos}⁡t=u,du=-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(9{cos}^{3}⁡t)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =9{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{3}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-9{\int }_{1}^{1}(u+{u}^{3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=4x\,i+4y\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+6\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =4x=4(8\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=32\operatorname{cos}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =4y=4(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=24\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-8\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(32\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (6\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(24\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-8\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }192({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }192\,\text{d}t \\  & =192t{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =192(2\pi -0) \\  & =384\pi \end{aligned}
$$
